fieldMarks: Smallest rabbit in North America, 246-462 g, 23.5-29.5 cm
Short rounded ears with white margins; dense hair on ears and feet
behavior: Only North American rabbit that digs its own burrows, with multiple entrances at sagebrush bases
Uses runways between food plants above and below snow
habitat: Big sagebrush habitat, secondarily rabbitbrush, at roughly 1,370-2,135 m.
range: Great Basin and intermountain West: southwestern Montana through southern Idaho, Oregon, northern Utah, Nevada, eastern California, with isolated populations in Washington and Wyoming.
